meta.title: PalletLab — Robotics with C++
meta.description: Learn robotics with C++ by building a palletizing planner: geometry, stability, search, ROS 2 and the systems around a real robot cell.
meta.inspired: Inspired by the work of industry leaders in Japanese warehouse robotics.

home.heroLead: Learn robotics with C++ by building the brain of a palletizing robot: where every carton goes, why it stays up, and how a warehouse decides what ships next.
home.hoverHint: Point at a carton to inspect it
home.problemLead: A robot cell gets mixed cartons on a conveyor and has seconds to choose a spot for each. A good spot packs tightly. A safe spot keeps the stack standing through wrapping and a truck ride.
home.rule1Body: At least 75% of a carton's base must rest on something, and its center of mass must sit inside the support polygon.
home.rule2Body: A carton may not crush a lighter one under it. The stack gets heavier towards the deck, so the center of mass stays low.
home.rule3Body: A suction gripper comes straight down. A spot under an overhang may be free, but the robot can't get there.
home.compareLead: Greedy fills rows and never looks back. Extreme points searches every corner the stack creates and scores them. Same 40 cartons, very different pallets.
home.ordersTitle: From one pallet to a whole shift.
home.ordersLead: Orders for three stores arrive all day. Pack them one by one and pallets ship half empty. Wait for a full wave and they ship full, a little later. That trade-off is the job of a warehouse execution system.
home.realTitle: Then the real world shows up.
home.realLead: Cameras misjudge a corner by a few millimetres. Cartons arrive dented. A safety fence opens. Real planners are built for all of it, and the docs walk through how.
home.stackLead: C++20 with CMake, vcpkg and GoogleTest. Eigen for poses. A real ROS 2 package. The same engine compiled to WebAssembly runs in this page.
home.learnLead: Twenty-three short chapters, each with a live 3D model next to the text.
home.inspiredTitle: Made in the spirit of Japanese robotics.
home.inspiredBody: This project takes its inspiration from industry leaders in Japanese warehouse robotics, whose intelligent palletizing and picking systems run real factories. Everything here is an independent learning project.
home.finalLead: No account needed. Read, play with the simulator, and ask the assistant anything along the way.
home.appsTitle: What a palletizing cell really does.
home.appsLead: Placing cartons is only one part. A real cell has to see them, grip them, stack them in patterns that survive the truck, and take pallets apart again on the other end.

apps.perception-and-vision: 3D cameras turn a stack into a point cloud; the robot finds each carton's top face and pose in it.
apps.grippers-and-suction: Vacuum cups hold a carton by pressure difference. How much force you get, and why it fails on porous boxes.
apps.layer-patterns: Column stacks are tidy but weak. Interlocked layers tie the stack together like bricks in a wall.
apps.depalletizing: The same robot, in reverse: unstack mixed pallets top-down without seeing the cartons' size in advance.
